text: We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated with Bulgaria, Albena Spasova told BTA (04.05.2026 17:27)

"We are fighting for the Cyrillic alphabet to be associated specifically with Bulgaria, moving beyond the popular idea that it is a Russian alphabet due to Russia's large population, as well as fighting to create our own fonts. It was truly important that the Cyrillic alphabet became one of the three official scripts of Europe specifically through Bulgaria, upon Bulgaria's accession to the European Union." This was stated to BTA by Albena Spasova, a lecturer at the National Academy of Arts (NAA), who delivered a lecture in Mexico on April 22 related to the project "The Letters of Bulgaria – The Alphabet of Europe." 

According to her, the presentation was structured as a "walk through the history of the global poster," featuring 30 leading authors in the field. "I had designed the lecture to include an introductory section about the entire project, followed by two slides for each author, which featured not only their poster for the project but also between three and five of their iconic posters," Spasova explained. She added that a "concise but very interesting presentation" was delivered within 60 minutes, which has already been published on the website of the International Triennial of Stage Poster. 

According to her, the sustained interest in the project is due to both the universal language of the poster and the theme of the Cyrillic alphabet. "The letter has always been a challenge for the poster artist... it is yet another opportunity to enrich the language of the poster," the curator noted. She emphasized that the collection brings together "the cream of the global poster world," with the participants' works being part of major international museums.

The participation in Mexico is part of a large-scale international festival in which Bulgaria was the highlight. In addition to the exhibition, expositions dedicated to Bulgarian cultural heritage, rose oil, and tourism were also presented. During the event, the Bulgarian artist Gredi Assa was awarded the title of "international honorary professor."

Albena Spasova noted that the event opens opportunities for future cooperation, including the participation of Bulgarian students in international initiatives in the field of poster and photography. She also emphasized the role of the Bulgarian Embassy in the realization of the project, describing the presentation as "glamorous and very impressive."

The international poster campaign "The Letters of Bulgaria – Alphabet of Europe," created by the International Triennial of Stage Poster in 2007, brings together 30 artists from 20 countries around the idea of a visual representation of the Bulgarian alphabet as one of the three scripts in Europe. The collection includes 30 posters—one for each letter, determined by draw during the fifth edition of the triennial in Sofia. The project combines the creative efforts of established global poster artists and Bulgarian authors, with one of the letters—"Ь"—created following a competition among young Bulgarian artists. All works are executed in a unified format and typography and are printed in several languages in a limited edition. The initiative aims to promote Bulgarian culture through contemporary art, transforming the letters into a universal visual code. The collection has been presented in numerous international cultural centers.
